Commentary.Commentary: Afghanistan, on the other hand, recovered really well after a not-so-good start with the ball. Mujeeb Ur Rahman got the early breakthrough as usual and Abdul Rahman followed it up with a wicket as well. However, in the middle overs, they were taken to the cleaners by Kusal Mendis and Sadeera Samarawickrama but once they got rid of that duo, they took control of the game. Fazalhaq Farooqi, Rashid Khan, and Naveen-ul-Haq all chipped in with one wicket each but it was the four-wicket haul from the experienced Mohammad Nabi that made sure that they bowled the Lankans out in the end, Now, it is up to their batters to put on a good show and gun this total down. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

Sri Lanka got off to a brisk start with Pathum Nissanka scoring some runs but Dimuth Karunaratne once again failed to make much impact. The game changed completely when Kusal Mendis came out to bat and started to take on the Afghan bowlers and punished them all around the park. He stitched up a brilliant 152-run partnership with Sadeera Samarawickrama and put the Lankans in pole position in this game. Mendis registered a stunning century and ultimately retired out on 158 runs off just 87 balls while his partner could not convert his start to a big score. After that no batter could do much and they suffered a collapse as they went from 257-4 to 294 all out which is an area that they will need to improve if they want to challenge quality opposition in the tournament.

A fine comeback from Afghanistan! It looked like they would concede a huge total at one point, but an excellent spell from Mohammad Nabi at the fag end of the innings helped them bowl out Sri Lanka for 294 runs. Kusal Mendis was the best batter with a brilliant hundred, but they will be disappointed not crossing that 300-run mark.
